problems.title: A union probability from a set difference
problems.question: P(A)=0.5,P(B)=0.3,P(A without B)=0.2. Find P(A union B).
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)-P(A\setminus B)$; $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$.
steps: The intersection is 0.5−0.2=0.3. The union is 0.5+0.3−0.3=0.5. No independence assumption is needed.

problems.title: A new die roll above an old sample median
problems.question: Six fair-die results were 2,4,5,1,5,6. Find the probability the next independent result exceeds their median.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: For six sorted data, median is the mean of the third and fourth values.
steps: Sort to 1,2,4,5,5,6. The median is 4.5. A new roll exceeds it only at 5 or 6.
Two of six equally likely outcomes give probability 1/3.

problems.title: Median, mode and mean from frequencies
problems.question: In 20 observations, values 2,4,5,6 have relative frequencies 0.35,0.25,0.2,0.2. Find median+mode+mean.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Counts equal total×relative frequency; mean is the frequency-weighted sum.
steps: The counts are 7,5,4,4. The 10th and 11th values are both 4, so median=4. The most frequent value is 2.

problems.title: A random point above a diagonal boundary
problems.question: A point is chosen uniformly from [−1,1]². Find probability x+y>1.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Uniform probability = favourable area / total area.
steps: The favourable region is a right triangle with vertices (0,1),(1,0),(1,1), area 1/2. The square area is 4.
The probability is (1/2)/4=1/8.

problems.title: The least quadratic sequence term
problems.question: Which term of $a_n=\sqrt2\,n^2-\sqrt{199}\,n+17$ is smallest?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: A convex quadratic is smallest at the integer nearest its vertex.
steps: The vertex index is √199/(2√2)=√398/4≈4.987. The nearest positive integer is 5.
The quadratic increases with squared distance from that vertex, so the fifth term is uniquely smallest.

problems.title: Circumcentre of a coordinate right triangle
problems.question: A=(1,2),B=(3,−1),C=(4,4). Find the circumcentre.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: A right triangle’s circumcentre is its hypotenuse midpoint.
steps: AB=(2,−3),AC=(3,2), dot product 6−6=0. The right angle is at A.

problems.title: Vector of an angle bisector
problems.question: AB=4,BC=5,AC=3. BD bisects B. Express BD using BA=a and BC=b.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: AD:DC=AB:BC=4:5; internal division weights the opposite endpoint.
steps: D=(5A+4C)/9. Subtract B to get BD=(5/9)BA+(4/9)BC.

problems.title: Cosine between two straight lines
problems.question: Find the smaller-angle cosine between 3x+2y=1 and x−y=2.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Directions u=(2,−3),v=(1,1); line-angle cosine is |u·v|/(|u||v|).
steps: The dot product is −1, and the length product is √13√2=√26. The cosine is 1/√26.

problems.title: Distance between two circle centres
problems.question: Find the centre distance of (x−3)²+(y+1)²=26 and x²+y²−2x−4y=0.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Complete the square in the second equation.
steps: The centres are (3,−1) and (1,2), since the second equation becomes (x−1)²+(y−2)²=5.
The distance is √((3−1)²+(−1−2)²)=√13.

problems.title: Combine two congruences
problems.question: Natural x<200 satisfies x≡199 mod20 and x≡99 mod11. Find its digit sum.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The conditions are x≡19 mod20 and x≡0 mod11.
steps: Write x=11k. Modulo20, 11k≡19; multiplying by 11 gives k≡9 mod20.
The only x<200 is 11×9=99. Its digit sum is 18.

problems.title: A vector’s direction cosine
problems.question: Find the cosine between 3i−2j and the positive x direction.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Direction cosine is x component divided by vector length.
steps: The length is √(9+4)=√13. Divide the x component 3 by it.

problems.title: Arithmetic-progression angles and geometric-progression sides
problems.question: Can a triangle have angles in arithmetic progression and sides in geometric progression?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The middle angle is 60°. With sides t/q,t,tq, the cosine rule at that middle angle applies.
steps: t²=t²/q²+t²q²−t² gives q²+q⁻²=2, so (q−q⁻¹)²=0 and q=1 for positive side ratio.
The sides are all equal, and the equilateral triangle does meet both conditions.

problems.title: Vector from a centroid to the origin
problems.question: A=(1,5),B=(3,6),C=(−1,7). M is the centroid and O the origin. Find MO.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Centroid is the average of vertex coordinates; MO=O−M.

problems.title: Negative terms in a rational sequence
problems.question: How many negative terms has aₙ=(n²−9)/(n²+10n+26), n positive?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The denominator is positive for positive n.
steps: Negativity requires n²−9<0, so n=1 or 2. At n=3 the term is zero.

problems.title: A geometric subsequence sum
problems.question: b₁=1,q=1/2. Find b₂+b₅+b₈+b₁₁+… .
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The selected sequence starts at 1/2 and has ratio (1/2)³=1/8; infinite sum=a/(1−q).

problems.title: From arithmetic to increasing geometric progression
problems.question: Three positive arithmetic terms total 21. Adding 2,3,9 respectively makes an increasing geometric progression. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Write original terms 7−d,7,7+d; a geometric triple has middle square equal to endpoint product.
steps: The new triple is 9−d,10,16+d. Hence 100=(9−d)(16+d), giving d²+7d−44=(d−4)(d+11)=0.
d=−11 would make an original term negative. d=4 gives 5,10,20, an increasing geometric triple of ratio 2.

problems.title: Optimize a product sum of arithmetic terms
problems.question: a₆=6 in an arithmetic progression. Which difference d maximizes a₇a₅+a₇a₃+a₅a₃?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: a₇=6+d,a₅=6−d,a₃=6−3d.
steps: Expanding gives 108−36d−d²=432−(d+18)². The maximum occurs at d=−18.

problems.title: Orthogonal vector combinations
problems.question: Nonzero vectors a,b have equal length and angle 60°. Find k making 3a+b perpendicular to ka−b.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: a·b=|a|²/2 and the required dot product is zero.
steps: Let |a|²=|b|²=s>0. The product is 3ks+(k−3)s/2−s=s(7k−5)/2.
It vanishes iff k=5/7.

problems.title: A dot product in a regular dodecagon
problems.question: In regular 12-gon K,A₁,…,A₁₁ of side 1, find KA₃·KA₉.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Vertices six steps apart are opposite endpoints of a circumdiameter.
steps: A₃ and A₉ are six steps apart, so A₃A₉ is a diameter. Its inscribed angle A₃KA₉ is 90°.
The dot product of the perpendicular vectors is zero.

problems.title: Two segments across a divided square
problems.question: M,N,K,P divide sides AB,BC,CD,DA of square ABCD with ratios 1:6,2:5,5:2,4:3. Find angle between MK,NP.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Use a side-7 coordinate square and test the direction-vector dot product.
steps: MK=(1,7),NP=(−7,1), with dot product −7+7=0.

problems.title: Cubic roots in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Find positive a for which x³−(2a+5)x²+(a²+5a)x=0 has three distinct increasing arithmetic-progression roots.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The polynomial factors as x(x−a)(x−a−5).
steps: For a>0, the ordered roots are 0,a,a+5. Equal successive differences require a=5.
The roots are then 0,5,10, all distinct.

problems.title: A geometric progression increasing from a negative or positive start
problems.question: a−2 and a²−2a are the first and third terms of an increasing real geometric progression. Find all a.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: For nonzero first term, q²=a; increasing three consecutive terms require positive q.
steps: If a>2, the first term is positive, and q=√a>1 gives an increasing sequence.
If 0<a<2, the first term is negative. It increases when 0<q<1, equivalent to 0<a<1.
a=0,1,2 do not produce a strictly increasing triple, and a<0 gives no real q.

problems.title: Sum integers excluding multiples of fifteen
problems.question: Find the sum of positive integers below 120 that are not multiples of 15.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Sum 1 through n = n(n+1)/2.
steps: The whole sum is 119×120/2=7140. The excluded multiples 15,30,…,105 sum to 15×7×8/2=420.
The difference is 6720.

problems.title: A geometric triple from two sums
problems.question: An increasing geometric triple has sum 26 and squared sum 364. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Let terms u,v,w with uw=v². Pair-product sum=(26²−364)/2=156.
steps: uv+uw+vw=v(u+v+w)=26v, so v=156/26=6.
The other terms total 20 and have product 36, giving roots 2,18. The increasing triple is 2,6,18, ratio 3.

problems.title: A purported necessary bound lacks an initial-coefficient restriction
problems.question: Every equation x²+bₙx+cₙ=0 has real roots. bₙ is geometric with ratio 2, while cₙ is a positive arithmetic progression. Which listed bound on its difference d must hold?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Real roots require b₁²4ⁿ⁻¹≥4[c₁+(n−1)d]. Positivity of all cₙ requires d≥0, but b₁ is unrestricted.
steps: Take c₁=1,d=0,b₁=2. Then every discriminant is nonnegative, disproving all listed positive lower bounds d≥c₁,2c₁,3c₁,4c₁.
Take c₁=1,d=10,b₁=4. Now cₙ=10n−9 and the required inequality is 4ⁿ≥10n−9, valid at n=1,2 and thereafter by induction.
This valid example violates both listed upper bounds d≤c₁ and d≤3c₁. Hence none of the choices is necessary.
problems.answer: None of the listed bounds is forced.
problems.note: The initial value b₁ is not related to c₁ in the stated data. A sufficiently large b₁ permits large d; the missing restriction makes every listed necessity fail.
